# Sanitized existing weekly payload

`livingston-lunch-2026-09-07.json.gz` derives from the existing local file `/tmp/knightbite-livingston/lunch.json`, found during the September 10 release-readiness pass. No Rutgers request was made to acquire it in this pass. Its filename identifies Livingston lunch; its menu type is `33316` (lunch). The original HTTP headers, capture command and an independent school identifier were not retained, so this is representative shape/size evidence, not authenticated upstream provenance or evidence of current availability.

The source week contains September 6–12, with `start_date` September 7. Its filesystem modification time is September 10 at 16:06:55 UTC, not a claimed HTTP capture timestamp. Source SHA-256: `9341369b6618b786e1ceb532d544cc90dc5fcc555b2e152d8fc7d2065e66925a`.

Sanitization preserves object/array shape, nulls, booleans, numeric values, public food/station names, dates, serving fields and label semantics. Auxiliary strings (URLs, sync/digest fields, descriptions and ingredients) are replaced with equal-character-length `x` text, preserving whitespace. Numeric IDs remain to preserve reference/variant relationships. There are no authentication headers or credentials. JSON whitespace reserialization increases the decompressed size from 6,551,705 to 7,065,491 bytes, so the checked-in fixture exercises a slightly larger byte budget. Gzip is only repository storage; tests decompress it before passing a normal response to the loader.

Both structures have 270,517 nodes, maximum depth 10, maximum array length 226, maximum object size 37, maximum string length 1,909 and maximum key length 33. All fit the existing bounds. Per-day food counts are 179, 192, 192, 203, 195, 178 and 176. The regression compares a full week against isolated requested-day results, checks those exact counts and unique identities, and never changes/truncates the accepted menu.

Replaying this lunch body through all three meal transports tests common code, not three independently captured meals. Still needed: independent Busch/Neilson weekly payloads; Livingston breakfast/dinner and another high-volume/seasonal week; full schools response; full Atrium menu and independently identifying label responses with size/transport metadata. Existing FoodProNet excerpts and synthetic stress fixtures remain useful but do not fill those gaps.
